newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber quiet, trade looks for direction.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber quiet, trade looks for direction.

text.p: Trading in the Singapore rubber market was quiet anew on Tuesday with the trade waiting for leads going into the afternoon session from Japan and any kind of buying by major consumers here, dealers said.
"We're essentially waiting for leads. That should come from Japan although some people are still nervous about the currency problems in the region," a dealer said.
Traders said the market was also trying to see if regular buyers like Michelin, Bridgestone or Goodyear will go into the market to pick up material as part of their weekly buying programme.
The market was also mulling the possibility Bangkok may be forced to sell some of its stocks soon as part of a rescue package with the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
"The talk is still going around the market," a dealer said. "It may take some time before it is cleared up."

At around 0445 GMT, September RSS3 was indicated at 89.00 U.S. cents a kg from 90.75 cents. October TSR20 was indicated at 91.50 U.S. cents a kg from 92.25 cents. September RSS1 was indicated at 137.00 Singapore cents (90 U.S. cents) a kg from 138.00 cents. - Rene Pastor, Singapore Newsroom 65-8703305, fax 65-7768112/- Email: singapore.newsroom@reuters.com
